newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African gold shares ended firmer on the back of a brighter bullion price, fixed in London this morning at a one-month high of $348.20 an ounce, dealers said.
They said the yellow metal's steady recovery since late last week had also been helped by some weakness in the U.S. currency.
"The golds have traded up slightly in line with the bullion price," James Scott, an equities trader at stockbroker Societe Generale Frankel Pollak told Reuters.
He added, however, that bullion's climb which saw it break over the $346 an ounce level on Thursday could be short-lived if the dollar livened up soon.
The precious metal was last bid at $350.10 an ounce.

"Well I wouldn't hold one's breath for it to hold. I think bullion traders will be watching the dollar quite closely and if we see further weakness in the dollar we could see bullion firm up," Scott said.
The gold index finished up 30.3 points at 1,267.9, while the industrial index was down 25.1 points at 8,476.1, and the all-share gained 6.5 points to close at 7,185.9.
Dealers said market volumes were moderate with 583 million rand worth of shares exchanging hands by the close of trade.
They said Tuesday's trading session was expected to be unchanged with market players eyeing Wall Street and some local economic data for further direction during the week.
The local March year-on-year producer price inflation figure is scheduled for release on Thursday.

Dealers said industrials were disappointed by Wall Street's gains on Friday and finished weaker on the back of some profit-taking and a disappointing start in results reporting by one of the industrial giants among several scheduled to release their results this week.
"Nampak's results came out and we saw a little bit more of a softening," Scott said.
Packaging group Nampak Ltd raised its first half headline earnings by eight percent and its attributable earnings climbed to 55.9 cents per share from 52.2 cents previously.

Its interim dividend was slightly more at 14.4 cents from 13.7 cents, but to add to market disappointment the company warned its full year earnings were likely to show little improvement over the year as sales volume growth continued to disappoint and margins stayed under pressure.
Dealers, however, said the overall market's underlying sentiment remained positive.
Industrial giant South African Breweries which reports its year result on Tuesday, finished down 125 cents to 133.25 rand.
Tiger Oats and CG Smith -- which are also scheduled to report their interim earning this week -- both finished down five cents at 25.65 rand.
Movers on the gold board included Vaal Reefs which went up 750 rand to 275.50 rand, Kloof which gained 70 cents to 32.50 and Kalgold which finished 15 cents up at 330 cents, dealers said.
South African gold share futures were also cheered by bullion, while industrial contracts were stunted on the back of a weaker long bond market, they added.
The June industrial contract was last at 8,323/32 from 8,385 settlement, the gold contract was at 896/902 from 871 settlement and all-shares were at 6,651/60 from the 6,676 settlement.
-- Ellis Mnyandu, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
